records.excerpt:
China appears to have built significant point-defense capabilities, in the form of large anti-aircraft guns and probable close-in weapons systems (CIWS), at each of its outposts in the Spratly Islands.

It's completely normal for us to build facilities and deploy necessary defense equipment there, a right of a sovereign state recognized by international law.

records.excerpt:
"We have seen evidence of surface-to-air missile deployments to Woody Island," a U.S. defense official says, in the first official public comments about China placing a weapons system on a disputed island in the South China Sea.

I want to stress that the Xisha Islands are China's inherent territory. China has been deploying various kinds of national defense facilities on the Xisha Islands for several decades.

records.summary: China deployed HQ-9 surface-to-air missile batteries on Woody Island in the Paracels, first seen in satellite imagery of 14 February and confirmed by US and Taiwanese officials on 16-17 February 2016; Foreign Minister Wang Yi described them as limited and necessary defence facilities and the Foreign Ministry said defence deployments on the Xisha Islands were nothing new. Fighter aircraft were also reported on the island on 23 February.

records.excerpt:
This week, Xiao Jie, the mayor of what Beijing calls Sansha City, an administrative base for disputed South China Sea islands and reefs it controls, said China planned preparatory work this year to build environmental monitoring stations on a number of islands, including Scarborough Shoal.

It is China's sovereignty to decide what to do or not to do on Huangyan Dao.

records.note: Not an assertive act: Sansha officials’ announced monitoring station at Scarborough was disavowed by the MFA as false within days, and nothing followed. Presence at Scarborough remains under CN201205.

records.suggestion_reasoning: First landing of strategic bombers on a disputed island is a unilateral military demonstration without confrontation; demonstrative, new in kind. [confidence: high]
records.excerpt: The People’s Liberation Army Air Force (PLAAF) announced on May 18 that it had landed bombers, including the top-of-the-line H-6K, on an outpost in the South China Sea for the first time.
records.sources:
China Lands First Bomber on South China Sea Island — CSIS Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative 2018-05-18
https://amti.csis.org/china-lands-first-bomber-south-china-sea-island/
records.summary: The PLA Air Force announced on 18 May 2018 that bombers including the H-6K had for the first time conducted take-off and landing training on an island in the South China Sea, identified from the published footage as Woody Island in the Paracels; Vietnam and the Philippines protested and the United States criticised the militarisation.
records.presort: new move (novelty) — First take-off and landing of H-6K bombers on a SCS island (Woody); 2017 had only fighter rotations there (ev-3560ee4bd1). [claude-code/opus]

records.summary: After the Indonesian navy detained the Chinese trawler Gui Bei Yu 27088 off the Natuna Islands on 27 May 2016, the Foreign Ministry said on 30 May that China and Indonesia had different opinions on the waters concerned, that the boat had been operating normally, and that China had lodged solemn representations with Indonesia.

records.summary: From about February 2016 China stationed four to five coast guard and other vessels inside the lagoons of Jackson (Quirino) Atoll and chased away Filipino fishermen who tried to enter their traditional fishing ground, until the ships left in early March; Beijing said China Rescue and Salvage of the Ministry of Transport had sent ships to tow away a grounded foreign fishing vessel and had advised nearby fishing boats to leave.
records.presort: new move (scope) — Excluding Filipino fishermen from Jackson (Quirino) Atoll extends the coercion of CN201402, which in 2015 was confined to Scarborough Shoal, to a new feature. [claude-code/opus]

records.summary: China's Permanent Mission to the UN circulated Note Verbale CML/11/2020 on 23 March 2020 in reply to two Philippine notes of 6 March, asserting sovereignty over Nansha Qundao and Huangyan Dao and historic rights in the South China Sea, declaring the Kalayaan Island Group part of China's Nansha Qundao illegally occupied by the Philippines since the 1970s, and rejecting the 2016 arbitral awards.
records.presort: continuation of ev-d73044394d (a candidate, provisional) — Note CML/11/2020 repeats the UN-note method of Dec 2019 (ev-d73044394d), answering others' notes (more to react to, not frequency); provisional. [claude-code/opus]

records.actors: China Coast Guard; Foreign Ministry spokesperson Hua Chunying
records.suggestion_reasoning: The protest and the first explicit official claim of overlapping maritime rights in Natuna waters is a verbal assertion of a new scope; declarative (coast guard dispatch noted but no confrontation reported). [confidence: high]
records.excerpt:
This incident took place in waters that are Chinese fishermen's traditional fishing grounds and where China and Indonesia have overlapping claims for maritime rights and interests.

But it is also true that the two countries have overlapping claims for maritime rights and interests over some waters of the South China Sea.
records.location_name: waters off the Natuna Islands, southwest South China Sea
records.sources:
Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Hua Chunying's Remarks on Indonesian Navy Vessels Harassing and Shooting Chinese Fishing Boats and Fishermen — Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China 2016-06-19
https://www.mfa.gov.cn/eng/xw/fyrbt/fyrbt/202405/t20240530_11349463.html
Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Hua Chunying's Regular Press Conference on June 23, 2016 — Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China 2016-06-23
https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/nanhai/eng/fyrbt_1/201606/t20160624_8525522.htm
records.summary: After Indonesian navy vessels fired on Chinese fishing boats off the Natuna Islands on 17 June 2016, wounding one fisherman and detaining a boat and seven crew, China sent coast guard vessels to the scene, lodged a strong protest, and on 19 June the Foreign Ministry declared the area to be traditional Chinese fishing grounds where China and Indonesia have overlapping claims to maritime rights and interests.
records.presort: same move as ev-7ad6eeb7b5 — June CCG dispatch and first explicit claim of overlapping rights off Natuna belong with the 2016 Natuna intensification led by ev-7ad6eeb7b5; the coder may prefer a separate declarative move. (group CN16-natuna) [claude-code/opus]

records.actors: Foreign Ministry spokesperson Geng Shuang
records.suggestion_reasoning: An official demand that Vietnam withdraw from occupied Spratly features is a verbal assertion; declarative. [confidence: high]
records.excerpt: With indisputable sovereignty over the Nansha islands and their adjacent waters, China firmly opposes certain country's illegal occupation of and construction of facilities on some of the islands and reefs of China's Nansha islands.
records.sources:
Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Geng Shuang's Regular Press Conference on November 18, 2016 — Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China 2016-11-18
https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/nanhai/eng/fyrbt_1/201611/t20161118_8525926.htm
records.summary: Responding to reports that Vietnam was extending its runway on Spratly Island, Foreign Ministry spokesman Geng Shuang said on 18 November 2016 that China firmly opposed the illegal occupation of and construction on islands and reefs of China's Nansha Islands and urged the country concerned to withdraw its personnel and facilities.
records.presort: continuation of CN198705 — Routine MFA protest naming Vietnam over Spratly Island construction continues the standing practice of publicly criticising rival claimants by name (CN198705, ongoing through 2015); one more statement is not a move. [claude-code/opus]

China, the Chinese government issued a Statement on China's Territorial Sovereignty and Maritime Rights and Interests in the South China Sea reasserting sovereignty over Nanhai Zhudao, internal waters, territorial sea, EEZ, continental shelf and historic rights, and the Foreign Ministry declared the award null and void with no binding force.
records.presort: new move (novelty) — Government statement of 12 July claiming maritime zones from Nanhai Zhudao and historic rights, and declaring the award void, is a new formal articulation of the claim; nothing comparable in 2015 moves. (group CN16-award-rejection) [claude-code/opus]

records.excerpt: Beijing injected an extra irritant into its long-running dispute with its neighbors with the South China Sea as it announced its annual ban on fishing in the area and vowed to stop vessels that drop a line into the contested waters.

records.summary: China's Ministry of Agriculture imposed its annual summer fishing moratorium in the South China Sea from 16 May to 1 August 2016, covering waters claimed by Vietnam and the Philippines, and said it would stop vessels fishing in the area; Vietnamese fishery representatives condemned the ban as invalid in Vietnamese waters.

records.summary: During USS Decatur's freedom-of-navigation operation past Gaven and Johnson Reefs on 30 September 2018, the Chinese destroyer Lanzhou conducted increasingly aggressive manoeuvres, warned the US ship to leave and approached within 45 yards of its bow, forcing the Decatur to alter course to avoid collision; the Foreign Ministry said on 2 October the navy had identified and warned the ship to leave in accordance with law. China responded similarly to other US operations in 2018 (Scarborough in January, the Paracels in May).

records.summary: On 12 December 2019 China's Permanent Mission to the United Nations circulated Note Verbale CML/14/2019 objecting to Malaysia's partial submission to the Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf for the northern South China Sea, restating China's sovereignty over Nanhai Zhudao, its maritime zones based on the islands and its historic rights, and requesting the Commission not to consider the submission; it opened a round of notes verbales by other states in 2020.

CN201207 [demonstrative, through 2015]: 2012, July: CNOOC offers oil and gas blocks hugging the western side of the nine-dash line, along Vietnam's coast.
